title: Flask Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Reply with text
examples.description: A route decorator connects GET / to a function. Its return value becomes the reply.

examples.title: Reply with JSON
examples.description: jsonify turns data into a JSON response. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Read a name from a path
examples.description: Angle brackets mark a path input. GET /hello/Ravi passes Ravi to the function.

examples.title: Check a path number
examples.description: The int converter accepts a whole-number path value. Open GET /double/4.

examples.title: Read a query value
examples.description: request.args reads query-string values. Open GET /search?q=cat.

examples.title: Read a JSON request
examples.description: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. The code checks that the body is an object with text title.

examples.title: Report a missing item
examples.description: Returning a response with 404 tells the client that this book was not found. Open GET /missing.

examples.title: Follow a named route
examples.description: url_for builds a URL from a function endpoint name. GET /start redirects a browser to /hello.

examples.title: Add a response header
examples.description: make_response lets you add metadata before sending a reply. GET /note has Cache-Control: no-store.

examples.title: Run a shared check
examples.description: before_request runs before route handlers. This practice check rejects paths under /closed. Visit GET /closed/books.

examples.title: Give a friendly error page
examples.description: An error handler formats a known error. GET /missing uses abort to raise a 404.

examples.title: Test a request in Python
examples.description: The test client calls the app without an open port. This example prints the returned JSON score.
